Version 3.4 has been much more stable than previous versions, however, I still run into user interface issues. For example, if I want to switch to a different book or resource while in reader view, I try to click in the top left corner, but 95% of the time, or more, it only brings up the instant details pop up or the verse tool. I have literally spent over 2 minutes just trying to change Bible books in the middle of sermon while trying to keep up with the teaching. If there is a gesture just for bringing up the resource selector, I am not aware of it. 

Also, the divider between the two text panes always changes position when switching between apps. I usually keep the divider halfway between my English and Hebrew/Greek texts. When I switch to my note taking app and then switch back, the divider has jumped to the ⅔ of the screen in English text and ⅓ in original language. That means every time I switch, I also have to reposition the divider. This is frustrating and should be easily fixed. As it is, sometimes, if I’m trying to take notes in the middle of a sermon or teaching, I don’t use Accordance, but use a simple Bible reader app, just because I get frustrated with the user interface issues. 

I hope OakTree Software takes care of this, because when Accordance works properly, it’s probably my favorite Bible app.

Best Study Bible App. After trying Logos, Olive Tree, Tecarta, and Kindle, Accordance is by far my favorite Study Bible app. Here’s why:

1) Broad Selection. I like to consider diverse perspectives. Through Accordance, I own and regularly access the following: 

Academic / Scholarly: New Oxford Annotated Bible 

Mainline Protestant: New Interpreter’s Study Bible 

Evangelical: ESV Study Bible 

Historical Context: Cultural Backgrounds Study Bible

Jewish: Jewish Study Bible (Old Testament) / Jewish Annotated New Testament

Catholic: Catholic Study Bible

Orthodox: Orthodox Study Bible

Devotional: Life Application Study Bible

New Oxford Annotated Bible, HarperCollins Study Bible, and New Interpreter’s Study Bible are the three in which I was initially most interested. Tecarta offered none of the three, Logos offered one, and Accordance, Olive Tree, and Kindle each offered two of the three.

2) User Experience: It’s amazing to be able to quickly toggle through all eight of my diverse study bibles for a given Bible verse or passage. It’s especially amazing to be able to do that anytime, anywhere on my iPhone or iPad. Kindle’s workflow is very clunky for comparing multiple study bibles. It’s been a year since I chose Accordance, so I don’t recall all the details of the other apps, but Olive Tree was the main alternative I seriously considered since neither Logos nor Tecarta offered the breadth of perspectives that I sought. I preferred the look and feel of Accordance to Olive Tree. 

3) Value: Accordance isn’t free, but then again neither are the other alternatives I considered. (Hard copies of these study bibles certainly aren’t free, either). One advantage of Accordance is that they regularly have pretty compelling sales. I initially purchased one or two study bibles to get going. I picked up the additional titles one or two at a time, as I found 20-50% sales on select titles. 

Another complementary offering is the YouVersion app. YouVersion offers no study bibles. However, it offers all of the translations/versions of the Bible that I want. For free. And for any verse, it’s easy to compare all my favorite options. Neither Accordance nor YouVersion meets all of my Bible Study needs and preferences. But together, they come incredibly close to accomplishing that!

Awesome Bible Study Tool. I’ve used Accordance for many years and have never been disappointed. It has an amazing array of resources, superior research tools, numerous ways to search for words, for grammatical structures, etc., and ease of use and speed of searches, etc., etc. I use it every day for both Bible reading and study. The app is on my iPhone, so I can read or study while waiting in the doctor’s office, while a passenger in the car, etc, etc.

Great for original languages. * Great resources that are tagged with the original print pages. This is extremely useful when citing information in papers.

* Accordance has great tools for languages. I've found the new interlinear support a fantastic resource.

* Always with me resources. Geared at simple to advanced Bible research.

* Resources often include the physical page number within the digital resource. This is EXTREMELY helpful when citing sources.

* The application itself may not be as polished as I would like, but their resource linking and their specific digitizing of resources IS what makes Accordance stand out above the other big bible software (Logos and Web based bible research).

* (update written 2019) I’ve used both Logos and Accordance now for different resource materials (e.g. - Lexham Geographic Commentary is only on Logos and Carta Bible Atlas is only on Accordance). I’ve found in general the following to be true: Logos is built to be a resource library. The library, and access to all of the library at any point, is the goal in Logos. They also have a larger digital library in general. Accordance is built to be a study tool centered around the Bible. The Bible is center and the resources aid Bible interpretation, especially with the language tools. While I wish both applications could be “combined” (a wish only at this point) I personally still point people to Accordance first, and Logos second. Ultimately, I think many pastors and Bible students will end up using both (especially possible since Logos 8 Basic is free).

Keep making the iOS app great!

I think the reading experience would also be greatly improved if there were an option to block-justify the text of my modules. Currently, if I turn my references off for a more seamless reading experience there is no indication of when a book or letter ends and a new book or letter begins (as far as formatting goes). It doesn't feel bogged down like my other Bible software.

Not optimized for iPhone 6. Horribly designed and poorly constructed. No audio. Not optimized for the iPhone 6 or 6 plus, which most of the other Bible programs are.

Poor attempt at what could be great. A metaphor might best express my view of this app. Here we have a scroll and are still awaiting the codex. It's a shame that this app so fundamentally flawed in its aim. The desktop app is great for grammatical research, which is not suitable for the iPad. The iPad creates a reading and note taking environment. Bugs in the code and in the logic make this app sub par. There is a lot of potential but as of now it doesn't just work.

Syncing Notes is Way Too Complicated. Overall, this is a great app and does what it is intended to do regarding biblical texts and resources for study.

The biggest drawback is the syncing of notes. This is a major issue to me because I use the app on both the iPad and iPhone and want to sync my notes with my Macbook and iMac.

Here’s the primary issue: syncing on the iOS app is not automatic. Instead, the user must manually sync notes both before closing the app and when opening the app. Compounding the problem is that syncing notes is way too complicated: It takes five taps to sync a note. This is unbelievable in an age where apps sync seamlessly (for the most part) between devices.

I understand there were issues with Dropbox sync that originally led to this, but the developer has not implemented workarounds that would make the process much less difficult for the user. For example, the issue could be addressed by simply adding an option in the note dialog box to sync the note to Dropbox.

Accordance is great overall, but the sync issue is a major issue to me. I hope that this is addressed in the next update.

Excellent Resource. I found the organization of the tools within the app very helpful. I especially like the addition of Strongs Concordance. The ability to select a word in the Bible and instantly bring up the etymology, pronunciation, and references is invaluable for study. I highly recommend this app.
